fields.name: Life story
fields.value:
Eleanor was born on a spring morning in 1941 and spent her childhood on her family’s farm outside Fairview, where she learned to love early sunrises and tomato vines. She taught second grade for thirty-four years and could still name nearly every student she ever had.

She married her sweetheart, Robert, in 1963, and together they raised three children in a house that was never quiet and always smelled of coffee. Eleanor tended a garden the whole street admired, never missed a grandchild’s recital, and believed that a handwritten letter could fix almost anything.

She is survived by her children Anna, James and Thomas, seven grandchildren, and countless friends who were made to feel like family the moment they arrived.

fields.name: Life story
fields.value:
Robert was born in the spring of 1938 in Fairview, the youngest of four. After serving in the U.S. Navy, he came home to marry his high-school sweetheart, Margaret, and spent thirty-eight years as a machinist at Fairview Tool & Die.

He coached Little League for two decades, never missed a Sunday service, and could fix nearly anything with a screwdriver and some patience.

He is survived by Margaret, his children Anna, James and Thomas, seven grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.

fields.name: Life story
fields.value: Dorothy Mae was born March 14, 1941, the third of seven children. She gave her life to Christ at the age of twelve and served faithfully on the Mother's Board and in the choir for over fifty years. A devoted wife, mother of five and grandmother to many, she never met a stranger and never let anyone leave her kitchen hungry. Her faith, her laughter and her sweet potato pie will be remembered always.

fields.name: Life story
fields.value: Biscuit came home in June 2011, a scruffy pup with one ear up and one ear down. For fifteen years he greeted every car in the driveway, stole exactly one sock a week, and never once let anyone eat a sandwich alone. He was a gentle shadow, a patient pillow and the best listener we ever knew. Our home is quieter now, but it is full of his love.
